questions.question: A statement and a budget differ in that:
options: A statement REPORTS the verified past; a budget ESTIMATES the planned future — and variances between them demand explanation
Budgets are drawn after the fact

questions.question: The cash budget answers:
options: The survival question — can we pay our way each month?

questions.question: The capital budget plans:
options: The purchase of long-term assets — machines, vehicles, equipment — separately from daily running

questions.question: Zero-based budgeting requires that:
options: Every budget starts at last year's figure plus a percentage
Every line starts at NOTHING and justifies its whole amount afresh — so dead costs die instead of riding along

questions.question: January's receipts of R20 000 comprise:
options: Cash sales R12 000 plus the collection of December's credit sales R8 000 (40% of R20 000)
January's full sales of R20 000, cash and credit

questions.question: The cash budget records a credit sale:
options: When the money ARRIVES — a month later, at collection; the cash budget thinks in cash only
Never — credit sales are excluded entirely

questions.question: February's closing balance is:
options: R3 000 — opening R5 500 plus surplus R3 500 minus the machine's R6 000

questions.question: The skeleton's fixed order is:
options: Receipts; payments; surplus/deficit; opening balance; closing balance — each closing rolling into the next opening

subtopics.title: Reading the Budget — the Decisions Inside

questions.question: The budget's "first gift" regarding the machine is:
options: TIMING — big purchases go where the balances can carry them, seen in advance
Hiding the cost from the bank

questions.question: If the dip had gone negative, the cheap-while-early choices are:
options: Delay the machine a month, or arrange an overdraft IN ADVANCE — banks price desperation dearly and preparation kindly

questions.question: The credit-sales lag means that when sales GROW:
options: Nothing changes for the cash budget
A bumper month's cash arrives AFTER its costs were paid — growth can feel tight in cash

questions.question: "A budgeted business meets its problems as variances" means:
options: Actual figures stand beside estimates, and every difference becomes an investigation months before it becomes an emergency

subtopics.title: The Wider Family and the Year's Close

questions.question: The capital budget feeds the cash budget by:
options: Supplying the landing dates and amounts of planned asset purchases — assets bought by plan, not appetite
Removing large purchases from the books

questions.question: Medium-term and long-term budgets differ in that:
options: Medium-term plans one to three years (expansion, staffing); long-term carries strategy beyond that, in broader strokes

questions.question: Depreciation never enters a cash budget because:
options: It belongs to the capital budget
No rand LEAVES — the cash budget records only actual money movements

questions.question: The comment habits for budget questions are:
options: A dip is a timing question; a deficit is a financing question; a variance is an investigation question

subtopics.title: The Month Written Before It Happens

questions.question: "A report is a mirror; a budget is a headlamp" means:
options: Statements look backward at what happened; the budget looks forward so the month can be steered instead of suffered
Mirrors are more accurate than headlamps

questions.question: The household page with incoming pay and outgoing rent, food and transport IS:
options: A cash budget — the same tool as Thabo's and the government's, differing only in zeros

questions.question: Writing the plan down matters because:
options: Unwritten plans cannot be CHECKED — the written budget turns 'the money just went' into specific, answerable questions

subtopics.title: Watching the Purse Through Three Months

questions.question: The quarter's purse runs:
options: Opens R2 000; January closes R5 500; February dips to R3 000; March recovers to R6 500
Opens R5 500; closes R3 000 in March

questions.question: February was safe for Thabo but dangerous for the cousin because:
options: The cousin paid more for the machine
Thabo SAW the dip on paper in advance and confirmed the purse could carry it; the cousin bought on feeling in a lean month

questions.question: "Earning and receiving keep different calendars" refers to:
options: The credit-sales lag — 40% of each month's sales arrives a month late, so a good month can still feel tight
The difference between wages and salaries

subtopics.title: Why Every Rand Must Re-Apply for Its Job

questions.question: "Dead costs love the copy" means:
options: Copied budgets carry forgotten, useless lines forever — the unused subscription, the outdated arrangement

questions.question: Zero-based budgeting "fires the whole list" by asking:
options: Why does this line exist, what does it buy us NOW, and what breaks if we cut it?

questions.question: The trade-off of zero-based budgeting is:
options: More effort than copying — repaid in found rands whenever honestly done

questions.question: The year's complete toolkit closes with:
options: Recording, posting, reconciling, adjusting, closing, reporting, analysing, costing — and budgeting: stewardship from spaza to state
